license.obligations: The MIT notice is kept in the header of the adapted file (attribution: React Bits / DavidHDev, MIT + Commons Clause). Commons Clause: the component must not be SOLD as a product — use inside a site is permitted.

preserved_intent: A wall of glyphs as a living background: a monospaced grid of random characters where every glitchSpeed ms about 5% of the cells change character and target colour, the colour interpolating smoothly (step 0.05 per frame), with a radial vignette over the top hiding the edges. The DNA is grid+flip+interpolate+vignette; the react wrapper is NOT carried over (a draft decision on the cross-framework port of the canvas DNA, DRAFT-GATES 2026-07-19 item 2).

replacements.glitch_colors: demo ['#2b4539','#61dca3','#61b3dc'] -> MATRIX tokens: --phos #22ff77 plus derivatives [#0c3, #22ff77 depths] from :root in index.html (the site's own phosphor instead of somebody else's palette)
replacements.characters: the demo ASCII set -> the site's GLYPHS (katakana + hex, the same set as in code-rain) — one typography across the effects
replacements.content: the candidate carries no demo text or assets — there is nothing to carry over

timing.mapping: the ticks are pinned to the same values as upstream (50ms/0.05) — the static-lite scaffold has no motion tokens yet; once a motion grammar exists the values move into tokens (a note for E05)

breakpoints.desktop: a band section 32vh tall under the hero, full density (charWidth 10 / charHeight 20)
breakpoints.mobile: the same section, the same grid density (DPR-aware), height 24vh — not a separate composition, the effect is decorative

reduced_motion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> the animation does NOT start; ONE static frame of the grid is drawn (seeded), and the section's content (heading and text) stays fully readable. The intake requirement is met in code, not only in CSS.
static_fallback: no-JS: the section carries a text heading and caption outside the canvas — meaning and navigation survive; the canvas is empty (background --bg) and nothing breaks.
cleanup: cancelAnimationFrame + removeEventListener('resize') + IntersectionObserver.disconnect in destroy(); the loop pauses when the section leaves the viewport (observer) — including on re-entry; no orphaned listeners (verified by motion-qa rAF-after-settle: a section outside the viewport does not tick).
lazy_strategy: island: the <script> module initialises on an IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 200px), off the critical path; budget: the vanilla port is ~3KB (against the 61.7KB gzipped react bundle from the intake runtime) — deployed inline in index.html following the scaffold pattern.
patch_set: PORT react->vanilla (draft decision): (1) useRef/useEffect -> a closure initLetterGlitch(container, opts) with destroy(); (2) props -> opts with the site's defaults; (3) [NEW] a seeded PRNG mulberry32(7331) instead of Math.random — determinism for ?visual-test=1 (the WSF-08 harness contract); (4) [NEW] a single-frame reduced-motion branch; (5) [NEW] an IntersectionObserver pause; (6) [KEPT] DPR resize, the 5% updateCount, the interpolation and the vignette — upstream's algorithms, identical in meaning.
